question: Identify another name of Choanocytes.
solution:
Source Code:

The correct answer is __**Collar cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Choanocytes**, also known as **collar cells**, are specialized cells found in sponges.
 
• These cells have a central flagellum surrounded by a collar of microvilli which help in the movement of water through the sponge's body.
 
• Choanocytes play a crucial role in **feeding** by trapping and phagocytizing food particles from the water.
 
• The structure of choanocytes is similar to **choanoflagellates**, which are considered the closest living relatives of animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sponges (Phylum Porifera)**

 
 
• Sponges are simple, multicellular animals that lack true tissues and organs.
 
• They have porous bodies and a unique feeding system driven by choanocytes.
 
• Sponges play an important ecological role in filtering water and providing habitat for other marine organisms.
 
 
 
• **Feeding Mechanism**
 
 
• Water enters the sponge through pores called ostia and flows through internal canals.
 
• Choanocytes capture food particles from the water, which is then expelled through an opening called the osculum.
 
 
 
• **Reproduction in Sponges**
 
 
• Sponges can reproduce both sexually and asexually.
 
• Asexual reproduction often occurs through budding or fragmentation.
 
• Sexual reproduction involves the release of sperm into the water, which is captured by another sponge's choanocytes and used to fertilize eggs internally.
 
 
 
• **Choanoflagellates**
 
 
• These are single-celled and colonial flagellate eukaryotes considered the closest living relatives of animals.
 
• Their cell structure is remarkably similar to that of choanocytes in sponges.
 
• Studies of choanoflagellates provide insights into the origin and evolution of multicellular animals.
